title: Workspace and AI terminal
summary: A developer starts work in an AI client and follows the same task in the proposed Status view.
preserves: Terminal observation, status feeds, worker roles, task dependencies and work visibility remain available within the existing ten-view dashboard.
enhancement: The client and dashboard share task identities and origin ownership, making prerequisites and waiting work easier to follow.
limit: Client hooks, controls and conversation visibility depend on the supported host integration. The terminal is illustrative, and worker activity does not mean that a result has been accepted.
question: Can you follow the terminal request through assigned work and waiting tasks while still finding the existing dashboard views and actions you use?
alt: Proposed Status view beside an illustrative Claude Code terminal, showing one running task, two waiting tasks and visible origin ownership.

title: Planning and the task board
summary: The terminal proposes plan version three while the Board shows its tasks and pending approval.
preserves: The existing board, task history, work controls and readiness gates remain part of the workflow.
enhancement: A unified view connects plan versions, linked evidence and explicit approval state so a reviewer can inspect the proposed work before it starts.
limit: All acceptance criteria in this example remain unchecked. Ready tasks still await this plan's approval, and the scope of dashboard approval controls remains open for review.
question: Does the plan make dependencies, approval state and the next step clear without losing existing board controls or task history?
alt: Proposed Board view beside a terminal plan proposal, with plan version three awaiting approval and all acceptance criteria unchecked.

title: Agent collaboration and evidence
summary: Shared task messages explain why work is blocked, with failed test evidence visible in Runs.
preserves: Run inspection, message feeds and existing review evidence remain available.
enhancement: Shared task identities, attributed messages and scoped visibility connect an agent's progress report to the evidence behind it.
limit: These are authorized project messages, not model-internal reasoning or unrestricted private conversations. Failed evidence remains visible and task acceptance stays pending.
question: Can you distinguish an agent's report from verified evidence, understand the block and tell which messages the current user may see?
alt: Proposed Runs conversation view beside a terminal explanation, showing shared agent messages, a failed test log and review waiting for evidence.

title: Connected teams and routing decisions
summary: North Hub owns TM-413 while its execution stays reserved at a disconnected Partner Hub.
preserves: Federation visibility and existing cross-hub work capabilities remain part of the product.
enhancement: Scoped cross-organization delegation separates origin ownership from partner execution, with optional Jev advice explaining routing suitability after eligibility checks.
limit: Current partner progress is unknown; disconnection cannot release the reservation or authorize duplicate execution. Jev cannot grant access, reassign work or accept a result. Its absence requires a documented fallback, and no measured savings or accuracy are claimed.
question: Are ownership, reserved work and unknown progress clear, and does the design explain Jev's advisory role and what happens when it abstains or is unavailable?
alt: Proposed Federation view beside a terminal, showing TM-413 owned by North Hub, reserved at disconnected Partner Hub and accompanied by advisory Jev guidance.

title: Result review and acceptance
summary: A finished worker supplies commit-linked evidence while origin-owned task acceptance remains pending.
preserves: Run details, review information and existing evidence remain available to the reviewer.
enhancement: Consistent commit binding and explicit acceptance state carry the same review facts across clients and hubs.
limit: The terminal acceptance request is an unsubmitted draft. The disabled dashboard button marks an open design decision, not a permanent restriction. Authorized services own acceptance; accepting a result does not merge its branch. Test counts and code are fictional.
question: Can you distinguish worker completion, evidence review and origin acceptance, and which dashboard review actions should be available through authorized services?
alt: Proposed Runs result review beside a draft terminal acceptance request, with commit-linked evidence, a finished worker, pending task acceptance and a disabled Accept button.

title: Plugin tools and industrial operations
summary: A declared industrial package provides read-only inspection of a simulated controller and attaches its report.
preserves: The IIOT views and existing protocol capabilities remain supported through the planned migration.
enhancement: Nested packages declare dependencies, installation rules and permissions while contributing domain tools and dashboard content. This example permits independent installation of its components.
limit: Other packages may declare different child ownership rules. Start, Stop and Write value require separate grants. This is a simulation, not hardware qualification. Trusted plugins come first; vendor and platform support and later untrusted-plugin containment need separate proof.
question: Are package relationships and read-only permissions clear, including the separate authorization and environment checks needed before equipment changes?
alt: Proposed IIOT view beside a terminal inspection, showing nested industrial plugins, a simulated controller, an attached report and disabled Start, Stop and Write value controls.
